henry.title: Gravity and Weight on Other Worlds
henry.intro: Mass stays the same. Weight changes with gravity. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: 📖 Read each chunk. Tap 🔊 if you want.
🧮 Find your weight on the Moon and Mars.
✏️ Fill in the worksheet. Try the rover bonus if you want.
links: NASA Space Place: What Is Gravity?
Read the first few paragraphs. Find why you would weigh less on a smaller world.
Scroll to the row 'Surface gravity'. Moon ≈ 0.17, Mars ≈ 0.38, Earth = 1.

passage.text: 🧲 Gravity is a pull between things that have mass. Earth's gravity pulls you down. That pull is your weight.
passage.a: The pull of gravity on you.

passage.text: ⚖️ Your mass (how much stuff you are made of) stays the same everywhere. Your weight changes if gravity changes.
passage.q: What stays the same on every world?

passage.text: 🌕 The Moon's gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's. A 60 lb kid weighs about 10 lb on the Moon (60 ÷ 6).
passage.q: How do you find Moon weight?

passage.text: 🔴 Mars has weaker gravity than Earth, about 0.4 times (a bit under half). A 60 lb kid weighs about 24 lb there (60 × 0.4).
passage.q: Is Mars gravity stronger or weaker than Earth's?

passage.text: 🏠 Home tip: jumping high does not change Earth's gravity. Games and videos can only help you notice how different worlds feel.
passage.q: Can a home experiment change gravity?
passage.a: No. It can only help you notice differences.

words: a pull between things with mass
how hard gravity pulls on you
how much stuff something is made of

handsOn.title: 🧮 Weight on other worlds (+ optional rover)
steps: Pick a weight close to yours, or use 60 lb from the chart.
Moon: divide by 6. Write it on the worksheet.
Mars: multiply by 0.4 (or take a bit under half). Write it.
🎮 Optional: Drive a rover (see bonus below). Predict which world feels floatier, then try the Moon and one other body.
handsOn.look: Mass does not change. Weight = mass × gravity. Weaker gravity → smaller weight → floatier jumps.
handsOn.q: Questions 3–6 use the chart and your math.

worksheet: Weight is: Circle: how hard gravity pulls / how tall you are
Mass on the Moon: Circle: stays the same / goes to zero
60 lb on Earth → Moon (÷ 6) ≈ ____ lb. Circle: 10 / 30 / 60
60 lb on Earth → Mars (× 0.4) ≈ ____ lb. Circle: 10 / 24 / 60
Weaker gravity feels: Circle: floatier / heavier
Can a jump at home change Earth's gravity? Circle: yes / no
Optional rover: I predicted ______ felt floatier. After driving I think ______ did, because ______.
henry.challenge: Use your real weight. Find Moon weight (÷ 6) and Mars weight (× 0.4). Which is closer to your Earth weight?
henry.bonus: OPTIONAL bonus (5–10 min), only if Regolith works on the grown-up's Windows PC: Drive a rover. Grown-up starts Regolith and sets up free play on a Moon site. Core lesson works fine without the game — skip it if it isn't working. Henry: Predict first: which world will feel floatier, the Moon or another body? Grown-up boards you in the rover. Hold W to drive a short way (WASD steers; Shift boosts). Press E to get out, then Space to jump while walking (Space does not jump while driving). Grown-up then loads another body (Mercury or Enceladus are fine; Mars is okay but has known issues). Drive a little and jump again. Say which world felt floatier and why (link it to gravity). Observation only — no measuring speeds. H hides help. Backspace or Home recovers the rover from a pit. Bodies that load: Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Enceladus. Frankie: Grown-up sets up on the Moon and boards. Frankie holds W briefly, then stops. Count a few craters. Point to what is light and what is dark. Skip if the game isn't working.

frankie.title: Floaty Jumps and Moon Looks 🌕
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: On the Moon, jumps feel floaty because gravity is weaker. Mass stays the same — you don't shrink! (About 14 minutes.)
steps: 🐇 Hop 5 times on Earth. Feel the landing.
👀 Look at light and dark on the Moon picture.
links: NASA Space Place: All About the Moon
Grown-up: scroll the Moon page. Point to light and dark parts.

handsOn.title: 🐇 Hops + optional rover
steps: 👀 Light parts are high ground. Dark parts are flat low land.
🐇 Frankie hops 5 times. Grown-up: 'On the Moon, the same hop would feel floatier!'
🎮 Optional: Grown-up starts Regolith on the Moon and boards. Frankie holds W a little, stops, counts craters, and points to light and dark. Skip if it isn't working.
handsOn.look: Grown-up: say 'floaty' and 'heavy' as he hops. Don't claim we changed gravity.
handsOn.q: Circle light and dark on your sheet.
